narration.text: Everyone has something to say.
But for a lot of people, saying it out loud isn't easy. Or isn't possible at all.
This is BridgeAAC. A free communication app that speaks for you, one picture at a time.
I built BridgeAAC for my sister. She uses an iPad to talk.
Apps like this can cost hundreds of dollars, and dedicated speech devices can cost thousands.
No family should have to pay for a voice. So BridgeAAC is free, for everyone.
Here's how it works. Every button is a word.
Tap the words you want, and they line up in the message bar. Then tap Speak.
The buttons are color coded, so people, actions and describing words are quick to find.
More specific words live in folders, like food, people and places.
Open a folder, pick a word, and BridgeAAC takes you right back home.
If a word isn't on the board, open the keyboard and spell it.
Word prediction suggests whole words as you type, so it's faster.
Every button has a clear, friendly picture.
BridgeAAC comes with hundreds of its own symbols, drawn just for this app, and they all work without the internet.
You can choose the voice that fits.
Natural voices download once, then run right on the device. So BridgeAAC keeps talking on a plane, at school, or anywhere without Wi-Fi.
Every board can be made your own.
Tap Edit, pick any button, and change its word, its picture, or its color.
You can even add your own photos, like mom, a favorite toy, or the family dog.
Already have boards from another AAC app?
BridgeAAC imports dot-C-E and Open Board files, and it can export them too. So you're never locked in.
BridgeAAC helps with the rest of the day, too.
A visual planner shows the day step by step, with a star for every task that's done.
Mood check-ins help people share how they feel, and get ideas for what might help.
And simple games make practicing words and sentences fun.
BridgeAAC adapts to the person using it.
There's a calm mode with soft colors, plus dark and high contrast themes.
Touch settings help with shaky hands, and switch scanning lets people speak even if they can't tap at all.
It comes in ten languages, including Spanish, French, Arabic, Chinese and Hindi.
And it's private. There are no accounts, no ads, and no tracking.
Your boards and messages stay on your device.
BridgeAAC runs on the devices families already have. iPad, iPhone, Android, Chromebook, and Windows, Mac and Linux computers.
On an iPad, just open bridgeaac.org in Safari and add it to your home screen.
BridgeAAC is free and open source.
Try it today at bridgeaac.org. Thanks for watching.
